title: Progress: The Power of Small Wins
coreMove: Shrink the next step until it creates visible movement on meaningful work, then let momentum compound.
sourcePressure: The chapter uses progress research, minimum viable progress, and minimum viable preparation to show why small visible wins sustain motivation.
chapterSpecificMisunderstanding: A weak run would make small wins sound like lowering ambition or celebrating trivial activity.

hook: generic progress: the power of small wins topic opener
tryThisNow: set a timer for ninety seconds...
make a list of priorities without a trade-off
generic say no to one thing today

exampleSpecs.domain: city tree-planting crew seeking minimum viable progress after grant delay
exampleSpecs.stakes: small verified blocks keep mission alive without fake scale
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: She plants and maps the first ten heat-island trees instead of waiting for the full grant release.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: Ten saplings stand beside a heat map.

exampleSpecs.domain: medical illustrator beginning a patient guide with one usable diagram
exampleSpecs.audience: artist frozen by full guide ambition
exampleSpecs.stakes: one finished diagram helps real explanation now
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: He sketches the single injection-site diagram patients need tomorrow before designing the whole booklet.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: An injection-site sketch sits beside a blank booklet grid.

exampleSpecs.domain: community choir rebuilding confidence after a failed performance
exampleSpecs.audience: director using visible progress, not pep talk
exampleSpecs.stakes: one clean entrance can restore shared momentum
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Before, they rerun the whole piece badly; after, she practices the first eight bars until the entrance lands.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: A score is clipped open to eight marked bars.

exampleSpecs.domain: open-data volunteer releasing one cleaned bus-stop file
exampleSpecs.audience: maintainer tempted by whole portal scope
exampleSpecs.stakes: small public release proves movement and invites correction
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: She publishes one accessible bus-stop file and logs the next cleanup instead of waiting for every route.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: A cleaned bus-stop CSV sits beside a route backlog.

exampleSpecs.domain: apprentice mason restoring one doorway after flood damage
exampleSpecs.audience: craft apprentice needing confidence through progress
exampleSpecs.stakes: one visible repair teaches the next step better than planning the whole wall
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: He cleans one doorway joint, photographs the result, and uses it as the pattern for tomorrow.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: A repaired doorway joint is dusted beside a chalk line.

exampleSpecs.domain: public radio newsroom drafting one verified wildfire update
exampleSpecs.stakes: minimum viable progress is the next useful public fact
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: She asks for one verified road closure update now, not the perfect explainer by midnight.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: A road-closure note sits beside a broadcast clock.

skillTargets: identify minimum viable progress inside a concrete scenario
choose the response that creates visible movement on meaningful work before motivation collapses
reject the generic drift: A weak run would make small wins sound like lowering ambition or celebrating trivial activity.
explain the trade-off using source-specific terms rather than generic productivity language

tryThisNowSpec: Choose one essential task that feels too large. Define the smallest useful progress someone could see today, then do only that next visible piece.
